<h1>Settings and layout</h1>

The browser's **Settings** page holds the choices that shape the surface
itself: how it looks, where the LaunchControl sits, how presses behave, and
which player you are. Open it with the cog at the top right of the grid, or the
**⚙** button when the page is showing only the view reference. The **←** at the
top left takes you back.

Almost everything here belongs to **this browser**: it is remembered by the
device you set it on and changes nothing for anyone else, so a phone and a
laptop can be set up differently for the same player. The one exception is
**Webapp pad input**, which affects every browser at once.

<img src="/assets/mseq/webapp-settings.png" alt="The Settings page: groups headed Appearance, Controls, Player, Accessibility, Sessions and Connection, with rows for Theme, Knob value ring, LC layout, LC side, Mirror LC side by player, Drag-across triggering, Webapp pad input, Active player, Note-name overlays, Overlay label size, Save / load sessions, CC mapping, Arp curves, Server mode and Session token" style="display:block;margin-inline:auto">

*Every setting at its default, captured on a development machine, which is why
Server mode reads desktop-mock rather than pi.*

---

## Appearance

**Theme** is **Dark**, **Light** or **Auto**. Auto follows the light or dark
setting of the device you are on. The theme button at the bottom left of the
grid cycles the same three.

## Controls

**Knob value ring** shows or hides a coloured arc round each on-screen knob,
filled to its current value, so you can read a knob's position at a glance. It is hidden
by default. Whichever you choose, the readout in the corner of the LaunchControl
panel shows the exact value of the last control you moved.

**LC layout** is **Auto**, **Drawer** or **Console**, and decides whether the
LaunchControl appears as the full console or as a drawer over the grid. What
each choice gives on each screen size is in the table on
[webapp.md](/documentation/MSEQ/webapp#where-the-launchcontrol-goes), along with the one thing
the choice costs you: the colour key is unavailable while a drawer is showing.

**LC side** puts the console on the **Left** or **Right** of the grid. Right is
the default.

**Mirror LC side by player** flips the side for player 2, so that the two
players' consoles sit on opposite sides. It exists for two players facing each
other across a table: with it on, each of you has the console on your outer
edge and the grid between you.

**LC side** and **Mirror LC side by player** only apply where the console sits
beside the grid, which is a tablet or laptop with **LC layout** on Auto or
Console. With the console below the grid on a phone, or with a drawer, they do
nothing.

**Drag-across triggering** lets one continuous touch or mouse drag press every
pad it crosses, which is the quick way to write a run of trigs or sweep a row of
values. It is on by default. Turn it off if you find yourself writing trigs you
did not mean to while scrolling or resting a hand on the screen: then every pad
needs its own tap.

**Webapp pad input** switches the grid on and off for **every browser**, both
players included. It is a single switch on the Pi, not a preference of yours:
turn it off on your phone and every other browser's grid stops responding too,
and turns dim to show it. It blocks the grid pads only. The sequencer tabs, the
round buttons and the LaunchControl panel all keep working, and the Launchpads
are not affected at all. Use it to stop browsers editing while you play the
hardware, for example with a phone on a stand beside you as a display. It goes
back on when the webapp restarts.

## Player

**Active player** switches this browser between **P1** and **P2** without going
back through **Select player**. As there, taking a player that another browser
is using moves it to you.

## Accessibility

**Note-name overlays** writes note names on the grid for players who do not read
the pads by colour. It works in the trig and note-arp views of the synth
sequencers, labelling each lit pad with the note it plays. Choose where the
label sits on the pad: **Central**, **Bottom left** or **Bottom right** (the
default), or **Off** to hide them. The same setting turns on the current-chord
readout above the round buttons in the note-arp view.

**Overlay label size** sets the size of those labels, from 8 to 16 pixels. It is
greyed out while the overlays are off.

## Sessions

Three links to pages of their own:

- **Save / load sessions**, described in [webapp-sessions.md](/documentation/MSEQ/webapp-sessions).
- **CC mapping**, which chooses the CC each CC-arp row sends. See
  [CC assignments](/documentation/MSEQ/cc-assignments#setting-up-your-own).
- **Arp curves**, which set what each velocity and duty arp value means. See
  [Arp curves](/documentation/MSEQ/arp-curves).

## Connection

**Server mode** shows how the webapp is running. On the Pi it reads **pi**.

**Session token** holds **Forget & sign out**, which signs this browser out.
The next visit asks for the PIN again. Use it on a device you are lending to
someone, or leaving behind.
